title: Tier-1 NexusLoop selects concrete TaskMemory and runtime-event SQLite stores from ambient env vars and silently runs with persistence disabled when unset (second selection path next to Tier-3 wiring)
affected_invariant: FRZ-CFG-02 / FRZ-CFG-04 (one canonical configuration contract; no silent selection) and FRZ-STA-06
impact: NexusLoop.__init__ calls resolve_task_memory_persistence / resolve_runtime_event_persistence, which read INTERGRAX_TASK_MEMORY_DB / INTERGRAX_RUNTIME_EVENTS_DB and return None when unset, so durable task memory and event persistence is silently off for any host that does not pass explicit stores. The same selection also exists in Tier-3 wire_task_memory, giving two resolution paths for one concern. The Memory doc and STATE-X do not name the NexusLoop path as a composition root. Whether production hosts always inject stores was not verified.
recommendation: Owner to decide whether Tier-1 openers are sanctioned composition roots; if not, require injection (fail closed in PRODUCT profile) and add the path to the CONFIG-X/STATE-X closed-world inventory.

title: CONFIG-X closed-world env scan is limited to inventoried surfaces; about 25 ambient environment reads in intergrax/runtime are outside its stated scope
affected_invariant: FRZ-CFG-08 (regression gates prevent reintroduction of hard-coded/ambient provider selection); CONFIG-X closed-world claim
impact: The semantic production scan iterates inventory provider-surface paths plus owner chokepoints of the 54 inventoried concerns; git grep shows direct os.environ/getenv selection of backends, webhooks, signing secrets and roots in runtime packages (interactions, notifications, sandbox, workspace, observability, capacity, events, task_memory) that none of the CONFIG-X gate files name. The certification's 'closed-world' wording is therefore bounded by the inventory, not by the repository. Another CONFIG-X gate not read may cover these surfaces (not verified).
recommendation: Campaign B: run the CONFIG-X gates and extend the discovery to all intergrax/runtime os.environ call sites, or record them as sanctioned deployment constants in the inventory.

title: Inbound interaction request verification defaults to a no-op verifier; unset or invalid mode silently resolves to NONE
affected_invariant: FRZ-CFG-02 (invalid required configuration fails closed or stays explicitly disabled); env-vendor-qualification rule 'missing mandatory configuration: fail closed'
impact: resolve_inbound_verifier_settings maps a missing or unparsable INTERGRAX_INBOUND_VERIFIER to NONE (ValueError swallowed) and create_inbound_verifier returns NullInboundRequestVerifier, whose verify() accepts anything. The Tier-3 shared interaction intake wiring calls it without profile gating. A typo in the mode turns Slack/Teams signature checking off silently. The verifier is described as a lab default; whether PRODUCT hosts override it was not verified.
recommendation: Fail closed on unrecognized mode and require an explicit verifier (or explicit 'disabled' acknowledgement) in PRODUCT application profile.

title: Tier-3 non-strict serving surfaces accept client-supplied tenant_id with a 'default' substitution while FRZ-TEN-10 is PASS; TENANT-X silent-substitution detector does not cover keyword arguments or field defaults
affected_invariant: FRZ-TEN-10 (missing/invalid tenant must not silently become global/shared/default tenant where tenant identity is required); FRZ-TEN-01
impact: In local_workspace_application the run request model defaults tenant_id to 'default' and user_id to 'default-user'; LocalWorkspaceRunService builds Task(tenant_id=body.tenant_id,...) from the unauthenticated body and substitutes `or "default"` for the run summary. The strict production serving tenant binding (single tenant-authorization decision) is optional in harness_host_runtime (applied only when a binding is passed) and only the governed_contractor application passes it. FRZ-TEN-10 is PASS with evidence marked 'scoped evidence only'. The TENANT-X AST detector flags silent substitution only for assignments to tenant-named Name targets, so `tenant_id=x or "default"` keyword arguments and pydantic field defaults are not matched, although applications/ is a discovery root. Not tested at runtime; whether the LKW surface is inside the FRZ-TEN-10 claim scope is unresolved.
recommendation: Campaign B: confirm reachability of the LKW /run route without strict binding; decide scope of FRZ-TEN-10 for reference Tier-3 apps; extend the detector to keyword arguments and field defaults, or require the strict binding for every serving surface.

title: CONFIG-X, TENANT-X and STATE-X have no architecture-tier owner document; semantics live only in qualification records (and a technical guide for configuration)
affected_invariant: Documentation pairs rule (domain-layer docs/project/architecture/<DOMAIN>.md) and FRZ-DOC family
evidence: E1:git ls-tree of docs/project/architecture at the baseline lists no CONFIG/TENANT/STATE/PERSISTENCE document; git grep for TENANT-X/STATE-X/CONFIG-X in docs/project/architecture and docs/project/technical matches only ADR-CTRL-X-001 and ADR-SEF-001
impact: Authority hierarchy places architecture docs above qualification records for domain semantics, but for three certified cross-cutting concerns no such doc exists, so the qualification record is de facto owner and cannot be cross-checked against an architecture statement. PLATFORM_CONFIGURATION.md is an authoritative guide under technical/guides.
recommendation: Owner to declare the canonical owner doc per concern (existing architecture doc, new hub, or explicit pointer to the qualification record) in DOCUMENTATION_MAP.

title: Memory domain 'ENTERPRISE CERTIFIED / CLOSED' (MEM-ENTERPRISE-CLOSURE @4db4bb69) is not a roadmap stage; roadmap certifies Memory only through EBH-2H/2I
affected_invariant: Roadmap decides order, status and formal closure (authority hierarchy)
impact: MEMORY_ARCHITECTURE.md carries a domain-level certified/closed status at SHA 4db4bb69 (an ancestor of the baseline) whose stage ID and SHA appear nowhere in the roadmap (grep for MEM-ENTERPRISE-CLOSURE and 4db4bb69 returned no roadmap hit). Roadmap-level Memory closure is the narrower EBH-2H contract-boundary certification (86fafaa2). Readers may take the doc status as a program-level certification.
recommendation: Qualify the doc status as domain-ledger scope, or add the closure to the roadmap ledger.

title: Memory platform wiring builds in-memory organization/session stores on the Mongo and no-backend branches; admission gate checks only the user profile store
affected_invariant: Memory doc: authority != durability; production admission for persistent memory
impact: With MongoDB selected and org memory enabled, the organization profile store is InMemoryOrganizationProfileStore; with no backend, session storage and the user store are in-memory. validate_memory_platform_wiring_admission is a pure gate on the final user profile store only, so session storage and org store durability are not admission-checked in PRODUCT. The Memory doc scopes production admission to USER/LTM/STI; the org-store-on-Mongo case is not described. Behavior confirmed by code reading; production impact not assessed.
recommendation: Document the in-memory org/session fallbacks per backend, or extend admission to cover them.

title: UAEP path skips canonical context assembly when context_engine or llm_adapter is unset; CE-01 fail-closed guard is not applied on that path
affected_invariant: FRZ-CTL-12 (Context Engineering: one canonical boundary); CE-01 canonical assembly pipeline
impact: uaep_executor assembles messages only inside `if self._context_engine is not None and self._llm_adapter is not None`; otherwise request.message is used unassembled. enforce_context_engine_when_provider_sources_active is called from tool_runtime only. CE docs describe 'documented hybrid paths'. Whether UAEP can run in PRODUCT without an engine, and whether CE-Q gates cover this branch, was not verified (E1 for the hypothesis, code lines read).
recommendation: Campaign B: confirm whether PRODUCT composition always injects the engine and whether a CE-Q gate asserts it.
